exchanges: Good morning. My grandchildren are staying with me this week and I already need a nap.
Good morning! Grandkids can wear anyone out. How many do you have staying?
Two. Emre is eleven and Leyla is nineteen, home from university for the break.
A nice age spread. Leyla can probably help keep Emre busy.
She does, when she isn't on her phone. She's studying medicine in Ankara, very proud of her.
That's a demanding program. You must be proud.
Their mother is my daughter Nadia. She works long hours so I help where I can.
That's a big help to her.
She's been so tired lately, and the doctor finally found out she has anemia. Now she's taking iron tablets.
Hopefully the tablets help her get her energy back.
I hope so. I've been making her lentil soup every week.
Lentils are a great choice, they're full of iron too.
My husband Yusuf says I'm fussing. He was an engineer for forty years and thinks everything can be solved with a chart.
There's a place for charts and a place for soup.
Exactly what I told him!
Sounds like you two balance each other out.
Our neighbour Mrs Lindqvist came by with cinnamon buns this morning. She's the dentist on the high street, which is funny given the buns.
Sweets from someone in that line of work, that's a good joke for the neighbourhood.
Emre wants to go to the park after lunch.
Fresh air will do you both good.
My son Kerem's wife Selin might come for dinner too.
A full table tonight, then.
She's been having dizzy spells for months. They told her last week it's vertigo, something with the inner ear.
That can be really unsettling. Hopefully there's a treatment that helps.
They gave her some exercises to do. She says they make it worse at first.
That's common with those exercises, it often improves after a few days.
Our other neighbour, Mr Petrov, has a new car he is very proud of. An old Lada he restored himself.
Restoring a car is a real labour of love.
He polishes it every Sunday. Yusuf is jealous.
Maybe it'll inspire a new project for him.
Please no, our garage is full enough.
Fair enough!
Ah, I was wrong before. Leyla isn't doing medicine, she switched to architecture last year. I keep forgetting because I told everyone medicine first.
That's an understandable mix-up. It sounds like she found what suits her.
She's always drawing buildings, so it makes sense.
Then it's a good fit.
What should I make for dinner for six people?
Something you can make in one big pot is easiest, like a stew, pilaf, or a baked pasta.
Pilaf is a good idea, everyone likes that.
Add a salad and some bread and you're set.
And yogurt. We always have yogurt.
Of course, it goes with everything.
Emre has his violin lesson at four, so I'll cook while he's there.
That works out nicely. You'll have a quiet hour in the kitchen.
He has been practicing very loudly all morning.
At least he's keen.
Very keen. My ears are less keen.
A quiet hour of cooking will be well earned, then.

questions.message: What did the doctors say is wrong with my daughter-in-law?
Leyla's still studying medicine, isn't she?
What does Mrs Lindqvist do again?
What does Mr Petrov do for a living?
I think I'll make a big pot of tea first.
